utterances.text: You're asking me how it was that I knew that these individuals were members of the 7th. The individuals who were or were not members of the 7th or any other unit are unknown to me. I don't know them. However, generally speaking, I know that a certain number of conscripts from the Bila area were members of the 7th. As to who they were, where exactly they were located, and for how long they had been members, I don't know. I couldn't possibly know that. When incidents took place, we sometimes received complaints which we then transmitted to the corps. The corps would then order the investigation that was then carried out by the 7th, and it was only after that we would become aware of fact that individuals who had introduced themselves as members of the 7th were actually not members of the 7th. As for the area of Kljaci, Alihodze, Zolote we knew that there was a certain number of members of the 7th, but as for the names, no, I couldn't give you have any of the names. I don't know their names.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I switch to my last topic. You mentioned training given by foreigners or by the Mujahedin. Will you please clarify this? What do you mean -- what did you mean by "training"?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: I was never present at any such training. However, I heard that a certain number of young men who were not of age, who had not been mobilised, or who had not been recruited reported to them for training. Their essential motive was to obtain a uniform and sometimes even a weapon if they became members of a specific unit. At the time this training was conducted, these young men would get food, obviously, and sometimes even small compensation, so I heard. But as I indicated, the issue of bread was crucial during those months in this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So local Bosniaks were being trained?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: A small portion of them, yes. However, this training was not a high-quality, specialist training. The individuals in question were children who had never held a weapon in their hands before that. So the training that was conducted in this camp consisted mainly in handling of weapons. You couldn't call it a specialised or very professional training, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You mentioned training in a camp. What camp are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: It was just a meadow in the vicinity of Mehurici, not far from the houses where those who had moved out from the Mehurici school were billeted in the hamlet of Poljanice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And the training, was it conducted by local Bosniak people or was it conducted by foreigners?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: I think by both of them. I don't have any precise information as to who conducted the training. We in our units were busy with our training, because you must know that a large number of our members had not done their military service with the former JNA. So every unit experienced daily problems with self-inflicted wounds, with inadequate handling of weapons, the problems with the range of weapons, and that is why we had all -- the whole range of problems involving lack of ammunition and so on and so forth. So we all had to conduct some sort of training. And even us who had been civilians not long ago had to have some training. But I was not aware of their training. I didn't know where and when it took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Sir, you said training by both, locals and foreigners. How could the foreigners talk to the local Bosniak population? Were there translators?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Depends on which particular individuals are in question. When you talk about the individuals who had arrived in the area in the meantime, they didn't speak the language, but some of them learned quickly. However, they still needed translation from time to time. Others were born in these countries, were Arabs, but had arrive at one point in time before the war in Bosnia-Herzegovina to study there. They knew the language, and they knew the area. In addition to that, a large number of Bosniaks studied the Arabic language in school and could manage a decent conversation. Were able to make themselves understood. But there were not many of them who were able to act as professional interpreters at the time, especially in the area of Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You said some of the translators had arrived at some point in time before the war in Bosnia-Herzegovina and were performing as translators during the training. Do you know anybody who -- by name who did this?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: I did not say what you just quoted. First of all, I never indicated that any of them had arrive as interpreters before the war. I just said there had been people of Arabic origin who studied in Bosnia and Herzegovina, who lived in Bosnia and Herzegovina, who started a family in Bosnia and Herzegovina before the outbreak of the war. That is what I was talking about. Second -- now, I forgot what the second part of your question was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Prosecution, please have a look at the clock.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: No further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Defence, following the

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to clarify issues?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just two questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Husic, tell us, please, if you have any knowledge as to which particular armed force was on leave on the 24th of April anywhere else.

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: I cannot have that kind of knowledge, not even with respect to members of the 306th.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My second question is the following: The foreigners in question, did they ever train members of the 306th, and did you ever visit the camp where the training was conducted?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: No. I never went to that camp. I was never involved in the training of the members of the 306th. And they could not be involved in the training of any members of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. I indicated several times that the young men in question were between 16 and 18 years of age, young men who could not be drafted according to the laws of the country.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, no further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness. I have a few questions at the end of this long day for you. You said that you were not involved in writing or -- the report on the events of Miletici, that you were not involved in an investigation. Is this also true for the report that has been made and the investigation that has been carried out for Maline? Were you also not involved in that investigation?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: The report in question was written by me based on the information that I had received from people who were not involved in the event. It was not our obligation to have reports containing all the elements that might confirm that the events happened in this or that way. And when it comes to Maline, there was combat going on. The combat went on for 20 days at the time. And the first information I received about Maline, as I've already said, arrived on the 12th of June. In the course of that one day I received different sorts of information involving different numbers of people, different locations. Only later on the investigation carried out by the military security services did define everything and provided more details. However, I did not follow the course of this investigation because I was prevented from doing that by the combat activities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: So there has been an investigation also by the security service, notably the assistant for security matters, I think. This was Mr. Delalic at the time?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: In the 306th Mountain Brigade, from the very beginning Mr. Delalic was assistant commander for security.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: We had a witness before you came, Mr. Siljak, who was also of the 306th brigade, and he said that the investigation into the events on -- that may have occurred in Maline was done by Mr. Delalic. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: He was assistant commander for security, and it was his obligation to do that. He reported to the commander on the events that had to do with the overall security and disruptions that may have impaired security. Now, who it was, with whom and to what extent conducted that investigation I am not able to tell you because I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: After these reports were completed, did you have any chance to read them at the time in 1993?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: If I had made an effort, I believe that I would have had an occasion to read them, but I didn't, because later on when I spoke to Mr. Delalic, I received from him oral information that undesired things had happened. However, such things sometimes cannot be prevented during combat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Did you by any chance -- I don't know whether you would do this, but did you by any chance read these reports before you came here in preparation for your testimony?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: What documents are you actually referring to?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: The two reports, the one that has been made on Miletici, and you name the author, potential author of that document, and the other report that has been made on the events in Maline. My question is: Did you by any chance prepare yourself for your witness statement today by reading these reports?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: I have never read a report drafted by the military security.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: So I take it you can't confirm whether these reports still exist, which would interest me to know. Do they still exist, these reports? Can you say anything about that?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm not in the position to know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Well, turning back to Miletici very briefly, I would quote from a document, but because there is very little time, I will not show it to you but just summarise what it says. It is a document of 27th of April, 1993. It is P576. It's a document by the HVO, and they say -- they write on page 3 in my translation the following: "The massacre in the village of Miletici was perpetrated by Mujahedins and local Muslims." And they go on to give some details on that. And then they say the following: "Osman Tahirovic brought Mujahedin's to the village in a tractor. After that, the massacre happened." My question to you is: Do you by any chance know who this person is?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: I don't know this person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: He was not a member of the 306th Brigade as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I am not in the position to know the names of all the members of the 306th. I didn't know them then, let alone ten years later. But since I don't know the person, I can't say anything about him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Now, it doesn't make sense in that person came in a tractor, how many people drive a tractor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Names are mentioned, and I have the same question, whether you by any chance, I don't know, remember those names. One is the name of a certain Vahid Jasarevic. Does that ring a bell or nothing at all?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: I don't know Vahid Jasarevic. I know a number of people whose family name is Jasarevic, but I don't know anybody by the name of Vahid Jasarevic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Judge Swart. Microphone for Judge Swart.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: The last name I found here is the name of Vahid Jasarevic -- oh, no. I said that already. Lutvo Malanovic. Does that say anything?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: It can only be Malanovic because Malanovic is a family name that exists in Mehurici. I do know a man by Lutvo Malanovic, but he is over 70 years of age today, so I don't believe that this is the same person. Now, if there is any other Lutvo Malanovic in addition to that person who is very old today, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Let's go to Maline now. I have a few questions on what you said about Maline. Are you aware that after the investigation you told us about in June, there was a new investigation in October of the same year? Do you know anything about that, about the same events?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: You don't know? Have you heard, by any chance, that in October, in response to a request from the United Nations, the whole matter was taken up again and that the deputy commander of the 3rd Corps, Mr. Merdan, wrote a letter in response to the United Nations summarising an official inquiry into the same events.

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: I was not aware of the investigation being carried out. From the time when the combat took place involving this incident as well, this incident and a lot of other details and this for a long time remained something that had an impact on the state of morale in our units. We did our utmost to perform our task which was to train the troops continuously to -- to explain the aims of our fight and the need for the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the civilian structures have peace and order, that there should be control in particular units, that members of other units should be prevented from moving about in the zones of responsibilities of other units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Now, let me simply quote a phrase from this report without showing you the documents. I apologise for the sake of time, but it's P174, and I quote the third linea of that report to you. It says the following: "Soldiers of the 306th Brigade and armed citizens who were not members of the BH army units and who obtained weapons through some private channels took part in the combat actions in the region of the village of Maline." I think you have said to us this afternoon that there was no participation in the fighting by Mujahedin, and I ask you also by not by other member persons who were not members of the army? Is that your -- what you're saying to that?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: I can't confirm this. Now, what the members of the 306th did and what was under our control is what I was talking about. However, after such a long blockade and everything that happened throughout the conflict and immediately after that, everything that was perpetrated by the Mujahedin and armed individuals who cannot be placed in many of the units because they were individual civilians from the ranks of the refugees or the locals, they would in huge numbers follow the army scurrying for food. Many of them were armed, and the problem of our police when facing such individuals lie in the fact that they had to engage in new combat, so to speak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Now, we really have no time to discuss this. I don't want to prolong the stay of the interpreters today. It has been a very long day. But let me simply say that I was struck by your testimony in comparison to this document P174, which is signed by the deputy commander, Merdan. And if I understand him well, he is saying these people have been killed in action, which is quite a different version of the events than yours.

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: This is by no means a different version from mine. What was under our control and what was in operation via Simulje toward Radonjici, Velika Bukovica and Maline were the forces of the 306th Mountain Brigade, members of its 1st and 4th Battalions, parts of the 1st and 4th Battalions. In parallel with that, villagers of a number of villages, especially the village of Mehurici, Suhi Dol, Poljanice, and Jezerci, set off to wage a fight of their own, and the fighting didn't take just one day. They -- the fighting lasted over ten days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now I'm turning to the Defence. Any other questions?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just two questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Husic, in 1993, were you in a position to see, read, or receive a document that the Croatian Defence Council would be sending to its Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: There was no way for me to see any document drafted by the Croatian Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The other Defence counsel?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. We do not have any questions, but we believe that the -- the answer that witness gave to the Judge Swart's question was not complete. The witness mentioned some villages.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but in parallel with that line. The reminder of the village and Maline from the east side or maybe not east, from the direction of Suhi Dol-Poljanice, there was a number of armed individuals moving. They were civilians that had never been members of any army.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. This is the clarification I was asking for.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then. Thank for very much for having come to testify. We have made an effort to finish your testimony today. I thank you. I wish you a happy journey back home. I'm going to ask the usher to accompany you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
